output.title: Give distinct wedding markets distinct landing-page context
output.angle_statement: When a wedding business serves regions with different visual expectations, a market-specific landing page can make the offer easier to evaluate than asking one page to represent both markets at once.
output.audience: Wedding photographers serving more than one region who are deciding how to focus advertising and landing-page content while managing a limited initial scope.
output.reader_decision: Check whether each target region has meaningfully different visual expectations or reasons to choose the business, then decide whether one page can represent them or whether to focus first on one market.
output.reader_promise: Leave with a practical page-context audit: identify the setting couples need to evaluate, check whether the imagery and offer represent it, and choose between retaining a shared page, focusing on a priority market, or considering a distinct page.
output.positioning: Warm · Lightbulb Moments / Education. Teach a scope decision before a page-building tactic; do not position this as a results case study.
output.why_now: Use the next advertising or landing-page planning decision as the editorial occasion, not a seasonal trend or a dated client event. No present market-demand claim is supported.
output.core_insight: Bounded inference: geographic focus and page context can be considered together. A distinct page may be useful when the buyer needs materially different imagery or offer context; a different location name alone is not the proposed criterion [C3].
message_spine: Start with the buyer's setting, not the number of places the business serves: ask what the page must help this couple evaluate [C3].
Check meaningful differences in imagery and offer context without assuming geography determines preferences [C3].
Choose an initial scope: retain a coherent shared page or focus on a priority market. Present these as options, not a proven hierarchy [C3].
Consider venue-specific context only as an untested application of the regional principle, without promising a measured improvement [C4].
output.audience_pain: Editorial framing to validate, not a population finding: wanting to represent several markets while being unsure whether a shared page makes each setting clear. Public content should pose this as a question rather than use the uncleared individual account.
narrative: Hook direction: ask whether the page represents where this couple is considering getting married, rather than merely listing service areas.
Problem: show a blank conceptual page with several setting placeholders. Do not reproduce or paraphrase the private discussion.
Main point: introduce a context audit—setting, imagery, offer relevance—before discussing separate pages [C3].
Decision: contrast retaining a coherent shared page with focusing first on a priority market. Do not prescribe separate pages universally [C3].
Transformation: describe a clearer scope decision the reader can make, not higher conversion or better bookings.
Invitation: bridge explicitly from regional context to the proposed venue-level application, state its untested status, then use the exact approved CTA [C4].

output.differentiation: The substantive distinction is the unit of relevance: the wedding setting a page represents, rather than the photographer's coverage style, a buyer's funnel stage or a campaign's financial performance. The mechanism under consideration is coherence between setting, imagery and offer context. The reader's decision is whether to retain a shared page or narrow initial market scope—not to redesign a whole acquisition system. Venue tailoring remains a separate, untested extension.

output.carousel_reader_job: Audit the context a landing page represents and select a defensible scope decision.

carousel.direction: Hook question: does this page represent the setting this couple is evaluating? Use a neutral page outline, not a performance claim [C3].
Show a blank conceptual page with setting placeholders. Ask what the page needs to represent. Do not use the private regional account or its market names [C3].
Audit prompt: identify the intended setting and check actual visual expectations. Show blank fields rather than regional stereotypes [C3].
Audit prompt: check whether imagery and offer context represent that setting. Label the relevance mechanism a conditional inference [C3].
Decision branch: retain a shared page if it can represent the relevant contexts coherently. Separate pages are not mandatory [C3].
Alternative branch: consider focusing first on a priority market. Use priority-now / reconsider-later placeholders, not the private focus plan or a completed rollout [C3].
Extend cautiously to venue context: ask whether a specific setting warrants distinct imagery or explanation. Label this proposed application untested [C4].
Close with the exact approved CTA. Include an adjacent readable caveat that venue-level tailoring is an untested proposed application, not a measured client-experience result [C4].
